rules.title: Statewide Rent Increase Caps
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from increasing the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over the course of any 12-month period. Rent increases are also limited to a maximum of two increments per 12-month period.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential properties statewide, excluding deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, units issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome), certain separately alienable properties not owned by corporations or REITs, and owner-occupied duplexes.
coverage.owner_condition: Exempts certain separately alienable properties and owner-occupied duplexes based on corporate ownership status or owner residency.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, school/university dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, units with a certificate of occupancy issued within the last 15 years (except mobilehomes), certain separately alienable homes not owned by corporations or REITs, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
